entry.title: SAP Document and Reporting Compliance
entry.content:
Hello Community,

For a customer, we are implementing an eInvoice interface in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud using the scope item 5XU - Document and Reporting Compliance.

Our requirement is to generate UBL electronic customer invoices and credit notes in S/4HANA Public Cloud, then retrieve the generated XML files through the standard API “Document Compliance - Electronic Document File” from SAP Integration Suite. The iFlow will then place the XML files on a remote FTP server. From there, the customer has a separate interface that submits the files to their approved platform (PA/PPF).
For this reason, we are not using SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition with scope item 78L, as our scenario does not require direct communication with an approved platform (PA/PPF) or tax authority : Customer requirements.

We have completed the functional configurations according to the SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud documentation, and we are now able to generate Electronic Documents from the source billing documents.

However, we are facing the following issues :
1) Error during submission of the Electronic Documents : When we try to submit the generated Electronic Documents, the status changes to error.

Error details :

  • For credit notes : “No SOA service name is defined for interface UBL_CREDIT_NOTE_TRANSM”
  • For customer invoices : “No SOA service name is defined for interface UBL_INVOICE_TRANSM”

2) API does not return any Electronic Document files : We've created the relevant communication arrangement (SAP_COM_0703) for the standard API “Document Compliance - Electronic Document File”.
However, when we call the API, no Electronic Document files are returned while there are generated Electronic Documents in the tenant.

3) API still returns no data even when documents are only generated : We've also tested creating Electronic Documents without submitting them, but the API still does not return any available files.

We've checked the SAP Help documentation. For On-Premise systems, we found references to the activities “Defining SOA Services for Communication” and “Assigning SOA Services to eDocument Interfaces”. However, these activities do not seem to exist in CBC for SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, and we could not find an equivalent configuration step in the Public Cloud documentation.

We found an activity called “Make SOA Settings”, but it does not seem to provide the required configuration for assigning SOA service names to the UBL eDocument interfaces mentioned above.

Could someone help on this topic please ?

Thank you in advance.

 

Kind Regards,

Arthur

entry.title: Portugal eInvoicing – VAT Number for One-Time Customer in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
entry.content:
Hi SAP Experts

We are currently working on eInvoicing submission for Portugal using SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. We are using a one-time customer to record all orders coming from our source system. 

We are currently facing an issue when submitting eInvoices through eDocument Cockpit. During the eDocument processing, SAP is looking for the VAT number of the one-time customer in the customer master data.

The error we receive is:

"No VAT number exists for customer <one time customer id>; Check master data."

As this is a one-time customer, the VAT number and other customer-specific details are not maintained at the customer master level. Instead, these details are provided at the order level. We can also see the correct VAT Registration No. on the billing document under the Taxes tab.

However, despite the VAT number being available on the billing document, the eDocument processing still attempts to retrieve the VAT number from the one-time customer's master data and fails.

We would like to understand the correct approach for handling this scenario in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

During our investigation, we came across the BAdI EDOC_INTERFACE_CONNECTOR and references to the Cloud equivalent EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD, depending on the Public Cloud feature/release. However, it appears that these options may not be applicable or available for implementation in Public Edition.

Has anyone encountered a similar scenario with Portugal eInvoicing and one-time customers?

Specifically, we would appreciate guidance on:

  1. How can we configure the eDocument process to use the VAT Registration No. from the billing document/order instead of customer master data?
  2. Is there a released BAdI or extension point in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition that can be used to achieve this?
  3. Is EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD or another eDocument BAdI the appropriate solution for this requirement?
  4. Are there any standard configuration steps specifically for Portugal eInvoicing with one-time customers that we may be missing?

Any guidance or references to the relevant SAP documentation/BAdI would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you!

entry.title: EDOCUMENT043 "E-mail sender missing" in eDocument Cockpit - Saudi Arabia ZATCA - S/4HANA Cloud
entry.content:
Hello Community,

We are implementing SAP DRC for Saudi Arabia e-invoicing (ZATCA Fatoorah) on SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, and we are stuck on an issue.

Issue:
When trying to send an invoice PDF to the customer via the "Customer" button in the eDocument Cockpit (or the equivalent action in the Manage Electronic Documents app), we receive the following error:

E-mail sender missing
Message no. EDOCUMENT043

This happens for both FI-sourced eDocuments (Accounting Document) and SD-sourced eDocuments (Billing Document), for Saudi Arabia (SA_INV / eDocument type) documents specifically.

What we have already configured and verified:

  • Standard Output Management email sending works correctly for the sender address (already used successfully elsewhere in the system).
  • We configured Output Parameter Determination → Business Rules → Billing Document / Accounting Document → Email Settings (DT_EMAIL_SETTINGS decision table) with the correct Sender Email and Email Template, and activated the rule.
  • We checked Define Default Email Sender Address and Define Email Sender Domain under implementation activities— both maintained correctly.
  • We checked "Maintain General Parameters for eDocument" — no email-related parameter found there.
  • We could not find a Sales Organization–level or Business Partner–level email field that specifically feeds the eDocument sending mechanism.

Our question:
Does the eDocument Cockpit's "Send to Customer" function use a completely separate sender-email determination logic from the standard Output Management framework — specifically for the Saudi Arabia (SA) eDocument scenario? If so, where exactly is this configured in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition?

Any guidance, or a pointer to the relevant activity, would be hugely appreciated.

Thank you!

entry.title: Turkey e-Delivery Note (e-İrsaliye) – LicensePlateID / TransportEquipment ID scheme separation
entry.content:
We would like to bring to the community's attention a legal change published by the Turkish Revenue Administration (GİB) in the e-Fatura Paketi update dated 24.08.2026, which corrects deficiencies in the prior package released on 27.07.2026 and entered into legal effect on 14.09.2026. The change affects the Turkey e-Delivery Note (e-İrsaliye) vehicle and trailer identification structure, specifically EDOC_TR_ROAD_TRANSPORT_TYPE1 and its related proxy elements, and separates the schemeID values that may be used under LicensePlateID and TransportEquipment/ID, which were previously combined under a single element.

Under the earlier rules, LicensePlateID could carry any of PLAKA, DORSE, DORSEPLAKA, YABANCIPLAKA, YABANCIDORSE, or YABANCIDORSEPLAKA. As of the current package, a Turkish-plated tractor or truck must be declared as LicensePlateID with schemeID="PLAKA", and a foreign-plated tractor or truck as LicensePlateID with schemeID="YABANCIPLAKA", while a Turkish-plated trailer must be declared under TransportEquipment/ID with schemeID="DORSEPLAKA" and a foreign-plated trailer under TransportEquipment/ID with schemeID="YABANCIDORSEPLAKA". LicensePlateID is therefore now limited to PLAKA and YABANCIPLAKA only, and DORSE, DORSEPLAKA, YABANCIDORSE, and YABANCIDORSEPLAKA are valid exclusively under TransportEquipment/ID. The same package also extends the existing plate format and type validation to TransportEquipment/ID, and changes the plate-mandatory rule so that plate information is now required only when driver information is present on the e-Delivery Note, rather than on every document as before.

We are encountering related XSD/schematron validation behavior in EDOC_COCKPIT and would like to ask the community whether anyone has already received or identified an SAP Note under CA-GTF-CSC-EDO-TR that addresses this schemeID separation and the revised plate-mandatory logic, or whether this correction is still pending on SAP's side. Given that the legal effective date of 14.09.2026 has already passed, we would appreciate any guidance on whether to await a standard SAP correction or implement an interim custom mapping.
@edoymaner

entry.title: 1099 Reporting (TY2026): CSV Output Misalignment and Pre-Printed Form Generation Process
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community, 

 

We are currently planning to migrate from the legacy FIRE reporting process to the new IRS IRIS reporting for 1099 filings. During our validation and testing activities, we have encountered the following issues and would appreciate your guidance.

Issue 1 - Misalignment in Generated CSV File

When generating the 1099 CSV file from the Run Statutory Reports app using the relevant Activity Key, as per the new IRS reporting requirements for submission through the IRIS portal, we noticed a misalignment in the CSV output generated by SAP.

For some records, the value from the “Recipient City/Town” field appears to be carried forward into the “Recipient State/Province/Territory” field. As a result, the fields for that supplier record and the subsequent data are shifted and no longer aligned with the expected CSV structure.

We observed this behavior for both 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC for company code US02, which are currently used by the business for filing 1099.

Please find the attached screenshot for reference. Could you please confirm whether this is a known issue with the SAP-generated CSV output and advise how it can be resolved? The expectation is that the CSV should be generated in the required format without requiring manual corrections by the business before uploading it to the IRIS portal.

Issue 2: Pre-Printed 1099 Forms

We also have a question regarding the pre-printed 1099 forms generated from the same reporting activity.

When executing the 1099 report from the Run Statutory Reports app, we would like to understand how the pre-printed forms are expected to be generated for 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC for Tax Year 2026.

We can see the pre-printed forms were getting generated earlier for the mentioned activity key as shown in the attached screenshots.

Could you please confirm:

  • Whether the pre-printed 1099 forms should be generated as part of the same reporting activity/run used for generating the CSV file.
  • Which option should be selected under “Documents for Generation” to generate the pre-printed forms. We cannot see any other format other than CSV or XML.
  • Whether any additional configuration or setup is required to generate the TY2026 pre-printed forms.

Currently, we are only able to generate the CSV for IRIS filing, but we would also like to validate the process for generating the corresponding pre-printed forms from SAP.

Kindly let us know in case you need additional clarification. Thank you for your support.

Thanks & Regards, 

Naveen Kumar

entry.title: SAP DRC Germany - Incoming Invoice fails with Document Type not supported
entry.content:
Hello,

We are testing Incoming AP Invoices for Germany. The invoice is received successfully from the Vendor but while submitting , it fails with 'Ack. Failed at Send.Acc.Point'. 

The Application log states '....invoice_response:3::2.1 is not supported by the Receiver with Peppol participant ID xxxx...' 

We checked the Peppol Participant Information of both ourselves and the Vendor in  https://peppol.helger.com/public/locale-en_US/menuitem-tools-participant as suggested by SAP in Note 3723871.

We observe that whilst we have the following document types enabled, our Vendor does not have them enabled. 

  1. Peppol Invoice Response transaction 3.0
  2. Peppol Message Level Response transaction 3.0

Does this mean that the issue can be resolved by asking our Vendor to enable these document types in their Peppol settings. Extending this logic, does this mean i need to check with all my Vendors and request them to do so? Is that the way it is supposed to work? What happens if the Vendor doesnt enable it - is there a way we can decide at Vendor level whom to send Invoice Response and whom not to send?

 Regards

Mohan

entry.title: StatusCode is ERROR for SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, France, S/4HANA Public cloud

I am implementing SAP DRC for France electronic invoicing in an SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

As part of our testing, we are using two company codes within the same SAP S/4HANA Cloud tenant to test both outgoing customer invoices and incoming supplier invoices.

The outgoing customer invoice process is working successfully. However, after receiving an incoming supplier invoice, we encounter the following error when clicking the Accept button in the Manage Electronic Documents app.

Error Code:
EDOCUMENT_FR_INV-084

Error Message:
Unable to find the receiver registration ID or status is not SUCCESS. StatusCode is ERROR

 

While investigating this issue, I found SAP KBA 3793041, which led me to review SAP Notes/KBA 3772370 and 3713986.

However, since we are using SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, I am unsure whether these SAP Notes are applicable to our environment and whether any manual implementation is required or supported.

I would appreciate your guidance on the following questions:

1. What is the recommended resolution for error EDOCUMENT_FR_INV-084 when accepting an incoming France supplier invoice? Are there any specific configuration settings or prerequisites that should be checked?

2. For implementing France electronic invoicing and electronic reporting via an Approved Platform (PA) using SAP DRC, are SAP Notes 3772370 and 3713986 sufficient, or are there any other mandatory SAP Notes that need to be implemented?

3. How are SAP Notes applied in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition? Is manual SAP Note implementation supported, or are the relevant corrections delivered automatically through SAP-managed software updates?

 

Thank you in advance for your support.
